style: Defensively disciplined Leopards built on a formidable centre-back block and rapid counter-attacks. Under Sebastien Desabre they prioritise structure over possession in a 4-2-3-1 / 4-3-3, bypassing midfield with long passes to release pacey forwards.
recent_form: Returned to the World Cup after 52 years, qualifying via the playoffs with a winning goal from Axel Tuanzebe against Jamaica. Opened Group K by holding Portugal, with Yoane Wissa scoring in a historic result.

key_players.name: Chancel Mbemba
key_players.note: National caps record-holder (107); commanding centre-back and the emotional and tactical leader of the side.

key_players.name: Yoane Wissa
key_players.note: Newcastle United forward and the Leopards' dangerman: fast and clinical, scored against Portugal in the group opener.

key_players.name: Cedric Bakambu
key_players.note: Real Betis forward and squad's leading scorer (21 international goals); experienced finisher.

key_players.name: Axel Tuanzebe
key_players.note: Burnley defender who scored the decisive playoff goal vs Jamaica; partners Mbemba in a sturdy defensive block.

key_players.name: Aaron Wan-Bissaka
key_players.note: West Ham United full-back providing Premier League pace and one-v-one defending down the flank.

historical_news: Back at the World Cup for the first time since 1974, when they competed as Zaire.
Qualified through the playoffs with a Tuanzebe goal against Jamaica.
Drew with Portugal in their Group K opener, with Wissa making history by scoring against Cristiano Ronaldo's side.

media_sentiment.label: positive
media_sentiment.summary: Strong narrative around a 52-year wait ending and a resilient, talented squad; the opening result against Portugal generated significant positive coverage.
